facts.text: The pinned name header defines ACTION_MOBILITY_MOTION as the relative ROS name mob/motion.
The pinned name header defines ACTION_GNC_CTL_CONTROL as the relative ROS name gnc/control.
The choreographer source includes the generated ff_msgs/MotionAction header.
ChoreographerNodelet binds the owned MotionAction server to ACTION_MOBILITY_MOTION.
The Motion action defines STOP, IDLE, EXEC, MOVE and PREP commands; MOVE is 'Move through a given set of poses'.
The Motion action carries a geometry_msgs/PoseStamped array in states and a reference_frame string.
The Motion result defines ALREADY_THERE and SUCCESS response codes.
GoalCallback rejects a new Motion goal unless the choreographer FSM is IDLE or STOPPED, aborting with NOT_IN_WAITING_MODE.
GoalCallback rejects a MOVE goal with an empty states vector with UNEXPECTED_EMPTY_STATES.
The STOP transition from STOPPED or IDLE calls Control(STOP), enters STOPPING, and reports SUCCESS only on CONTROL_SUCCESS.
The CONTROLLING/GOAL_CANCEL transition returns CANCELLED rather than sending a Control STOP goal.
Result() handles CANCELLED and PREEMPTED by calling client_c_.CancelGoal() in CONTROLLING; it does not command a stop there.
SetStateCallback for mob/set_state calls fsm_.SetState(req.state) and then sets res.success true without calling Control().
The choreographer transforms MOVE states from a non-empty reference_frame into the world frame before planning.
The pinned name header defines the world frame name as world.
The pinned name header defines TOPIC_MOBILITY_SEGMENT as mob/choreographer/segment.
The choreographer advertises a latched nav_msgs/Path on TOPIC_MOBILITY_SEGMENT.
The choreographer publishes the segment Path with the world frame and its current timestamp.
The Control action defines STOP, IDLE and NOMINAL commands and the SUCCESS response code.
The control source includes the generated ff_msgs/ControlAction header.
On a Control STOP goal, Ctl::GoalCallback calls Command(MODE_STOP) and then updates the FSM with GOAL_STOP.
The WAITING/GOAL_STOP transition calls Command(MODE_STOP) and returns STOPPING.
Ctl checks the EKF velocity and omega magnitudes against stopping thresholds and only then updates GOAL_COMPLETE.
The STOPPING/GOAL_COMPLETE transition returns SUCCESS.
Ctl::Result sends a SUCCESS native action result when response is SUCCESS.

determinism.notes: Event-driven canned replies; no physics step, pacing or state-hash replay

fidelity.engine: analytic:ROS action contract stand-in (no free-flyer dynamics)
gaps: the fake answers the declared actionlib goal/result/status wrapper topics and runs no Gazebo, free-flyer dynamics, propulsion, localization, mapper/planner, TF or ROS graph
the MOVE result is immediate and canned; it does not model planning, validation, replanning, trajectory timing or the ALREADY_THERE response
the STOP result does not model the controller's configured stopping thresholds, latency or the EKF updates that establish sensed quiescence
the package does not launch or configure the upstream simulator, rosbridge, TF, flight modes or keep-in/keep-out zones; those remain deployment requirements
the MOVE position leaves require an operator workspace overlay; the supplied example contains fake test values only, not flight-mode hard limits or installed keep-in zones
native namespace and flight-mode selection, EKF/use_truth settings, child-controller ordering and overlap with retained Motion work remain unverified deployment blockers
the package exposes only Motion MOVE and the Control STOP safety action; IDLE, EXEC, PREP, mob/set_state, validate, reset and the other mobility services are out of scope
the fake's replies and state values are test data, not measurements or timings

safe_state.description: The fixed gnc/control STOP action commands the GNC controller's MODE_STOP and reports SUCCESS only after its EKF velocity and omega magnitudes fall below the configured stopping thresholds; this is an acknowledged native software stop, not a physical emergency stop.
